<reason>B won the load-bearing comparison: extra pouring hours add drinks on top of pre-loading rather than relocating a fixed appetite into a safer room, so the surge is larger and drunker, not merely better supervised. B also kept the motion’s “mainly” live by distinguishing an exit pulse timed to last call from an all-night grid that staffs peak-BAC hours. A’s opening and first rebuttal were excellent, but A never claimed a shorter night, overread B’s timed corridor as a concession of the proposition, and closed as if B had named no displacement mechanism after B had (friction, last-entry, hosting cost).</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s R2/closing: late trains do not relocate a fixed crowd; they subsidize extra rounds, so a lit 4am platform is a manufactured crush, and an exit pulse serves closing rather than replacing it as the main tool.</best_rebuttal>
